Subject: MAP: Performance evaluation & long-window / KV-cache benchmark

Hi Oliver / Emma —

Attaching the MAP worksheet (20261014_map_eval_plan.xlsx) and a short evaluation plan we discussed on the call. High level: HelioCloud needs predictable latency at large context windows (32k+) for the agent workflows; we want to include the plan & results in the MAP so legal/procurement have a clear close timeline tied to benchmarks.

Core evaluation buckets (summary):
- Latency: P50 / P95 per model variant (baseline single-GPU and quantized runner)
- Throughput: tokens/sec and sustained throughput at concurrent request levels (1, 4, 8, 16)
- TTFT: time-to-first-token under cold vs warmed KV cache (0, 1 warm request, steady-state)
- Max sequence tests: 16k / 32k / 48k / 65k prompt lengths — measure memory, latency step-up, and failure modes
- KV cache impact: cold vs hot, cache hit rates, incremental TTFT improvements
- Prompt distribution: mix of short (<=512), medium (512-8k), and long (8k-32k) to reflect HelioCloud's agent mix

Deliverables & timeline proposal (MAP row):
- 10/14: MAP with eval plan (this email + spreadsheet)
- 10/16–10/18: HelioCloud runs tests / Redwood provides runner configs to reproduce
- 10/19: Redwood consolidates results into summary PDF and final MAP row for legal
- 10/21: Executive review + signoff (target close)

Ask: can you confirm your test window (we put 10/16–10/18) and whether you can share a 3–4 sample prompts set (can be obfuscated) so we can reproduce exact distribution?

Thanks —
Dylan

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@heliocloud.com>

Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance evaluation & long-window / KV-cache benchmark

Dylan —

Thanks for the plan. We kicked off the runs this morning. Quick summary from our infra team (see attached summary PDF and CSV):

- Test bed: 4x A100 (40GB) dedicated nodes; Redwood-provided runner with quantization flag on for the "q4" variant.
- Max seq observations: stable up to 48k for our prompt mix; at 65k we saw multiple OOMs in peak concurrency (16) unless KV cache warm was used and batch size reduced.
- Latency: single-request P50 =~ 120ms (16k), P95 =~ 420ms (16k). At 48k P95 jumped to ~1.2s.
- Throughput: tokens/sec drops non-linearly after 32k; sustained throughput at concurrency=8 was ~18k tokens/sec (16k avg prompt), but only ~7k tokens/sec at sustained 48k.
- TTFT: cold = 280ms median, warmed (after 1 warm request) = 110ms median for 16k. For 48k cold TTFT spiked to ~650ms, warmed ~230ms.
- KV cache: warm cache gave best latency stability and reduced variance substantially; cold-starts are the main contributor to tail latency. CSV has per-run numbers (kvcache-comparison.csv).

We attached: 20261018_longwindow_results-summary.pdf and kvcache-comparison.csv.

Next: we can export the prompt samples (obfuscated) by EOD today. We can also do a focused run with your runner configs (send the exact flags you want).

Regards,
Oliver
Head of Platform, HelioCloud
oliver.grant@heliocloud.com
